chapters.title: Chapter 5: Owning Real Estate Without Buying Property

lessons.title: Real Estate Stocks, Mutual Funds and AIFs

children.text: REITs are not the only way to own a piece of Indian real estate through the stock market. You can buy shares of the developers building Mumbai's towers, a low-cost ETF holding the biggest of them, a new index fund mixing REITs with developers, or, if you have ₹1 crore to spare, a private fund lending to or investing in housing projects. These routes look similar on the surface. Underneath, they are bets on completely different things. This lesson shows you what you are really buying with each.

body.text: A REIT is a bet on rent. A developer stock is a bet on a business that buys land, builds and sells, which is why it can swing far more than the property market itself, in both directions.

markDefs.definition: The value of homes or units booked by customers during a period, whether or not construction is complete. The main sales metric Indian developers report.
Recurring rental income from assets a company owns and leases out, such as offices or malls, as opposed to one-time income from selling homes.

children.text: Listed real estate companies fall into two broad types. Residential developers like Godrej Properties, Lodha, Prestige and Signature Global earn most of their money by selling homes, and are judged on
. Companies like Phoenix Mills, which owns malls, lean on
from rent. Many, like DLF, combine both. The mix matters: rental businesses behave more steadily, while home sales swing with the property cycle.

body.caption: FY26 sales bookings of India's largest listed developers

body.title: Sales bookings, FY25 vs FY26 (₹ crore)
Growth in bookings
body.prompt: Prestige Estates' sales bookings rose from ₹17,023 crore in FY25 to ₹30,024 crore in FY26. What was the percentage growth? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: (₹30,024 ÷ ₹17,023) minus 1 = 0.764, or 76.4%. Strong bookings are a good sign, but bookings are not profit. The company still has to build, deliver and collect payments, often over several years.

body.title: Measure the swing
body.prompt: Over the 52 weeks to September 2026, the Nifty Realty index traded between a low of 638.65 and a high of 974.50. By what percentage did it rise from its low to its high? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: (974.50 ÷ 638.65) minus 1 = 0.526, or 52.6%. A 50% swing in a single year is common for realty stocks, while RBI data showed house prices growing only a few percent a year. Developer stocks magnify the property cycle.

markDefs.definition: Land a developer owns or controls for future projects. It can be a hidden source of value or a costly burden, depending on location and debt used to buy it.

children.text: Why do developer stocks move so much more than property prices? Four reasons. Developers borrow heavily, so small changes in sales hit profits hard. Their value depends on future launches and

, which the market re-prices quickly when sentiment changes. They are very sensitive to interest rates, which affect both their borrowing costs and their buyers' EMIs. And like all stocks, they are priced daily, so every change in outlook shows up immediately. In the 2008 downturn, many Indian realty stocks lost the large majority of their value within a year.

children.text: Route 2: Realty ETFs, Index Funds and Mutual Funds

If picking individual developers feels risky, you can buy the whole sector through a fund. The main benchmark is NSE's Nifty Realty index, and it is quite concentrated: a handful of large developers make up most of its weight.

body.caption: Fund routes into listed real estate

cells: Developer stocks in the Nifty Realty index
Low-cost sector exposure, traded like a share
Nippon India Nifty Realty Index Fund
The same basket, bought through a mutual fund

At least 60% REITs, the rest real estate companies
A blend of rental income and developer growth
Small, variable holdings in realty stocks
Incidental exposure without a sector bet

body.text: A realty ETF is diversified across companies, but not across sectors. When interest rates rise or home sales slow, almost every developer falls together. Sector funds suit a small, deliberate slice of a portfolio, not a core holding. Also note that a Nifty Realty fund holds developers, not buildings, so it will behave very differently from a rented flat or a REIT.

markDefs.definition: Loans to developers with customised terms, such as fixed interest plus a share of project sales, usually secured against land or project cash flows.

children.text: Real estate Alternative Investment Funds are SEBI-registered Category II AIFs that invest privately in real estate. They typically require a minimum commitment of ₹1 crore and lock money in for several years. The most common strategy in India is

to developers, often to fund land purchases, approvals or the last stage of construction. Others take equity stakes in projects, or buy and lease commercial assets. The government-backed SWAMIH Fund, which finances stalled housing projects, is itself a Category II AIF.

cells: Interest and fees from developer loans, sometimes with a share of sales
Developer default, slow sales, weak collateral
Share of profits when homes are sold
Construction delays, price falls, approval problems
Rent plus an eventual sale of the asset

body.text: Headline target returns in real estate AIF pitches, such as "18% to 20% IRR," reflect real risk: these funds often lend to developers who cannot easily borrow from banks. Fees usually include a management fee plus a share of profits above a hurdle rate, and returns come unevenly over the fund's life. Our separate course on AIFs covers fees, IRR and due diligence in detail.

body.title: Match the goal to the route
body.question: Ananya wants regular income from Grade A offices, daily liquidity and a small starting amount. Which route fits best?
options: Listed REIT units or a REIT-focused index fund
A real estate AIF doing structured debt
body.explanation: REITs are built for rental income from completed commercial assets and must distribute most of their cash. Realty ETFs and developer stocks pay small dividends and are driven by home sales, while an AIF needs ₹1 crore and locks money in.

body.title: The developer's sales metric
body.textWithBlank: Indian developers report the value of homes booked by customers in a period as ___-sales, even before construction is complete.
body.explanation: Pre-sales, also called sales bookings, show demand. Investors should also check collections, since bookings only become cash as buyers pay instalments.

body.title: The 18% real estate AIF pitch
body.scenario: Mr and Mrs Kapoor, business owners in Ludhiana, have a ₹6 crore portfolio: ₹3 crore in property, ₹2 crore in equity mutual funds and ₹1 crore in FDs. A wealth manager pitches a real estate structured debt AIF: ₹1 crore minimum, 5-year tenure, "target IRR of 18%, secured by land."
body.prompt: What should the Kapoors think through before committing?
body.modelAnswer:
1. Concentration: they already hold ₹3 crore, or 50%, in property. Adding ₹1 crore of real estate AIF takes real estate exposure to about ₹4 crore of ₹6 crore, roughly 67%, and it would come mostly out of their liquid FDs or equity.
2. Why 18%: high target returns mean the fund lends to developers who pay more because banks will not lend to them cheaply. "Secured by land" helps only if the land can be sold quickly at a fair value, which is rarely easy.
3. Target, not guarantee: an IRR target can be missed, and delays are common in developer lending.
4. Liquidity: the money is locked for about 5 years, possibly with extensions, and they cannot easily exit early.
5. Fees and tax: they should get the full fee structure in writing and understand how Category II AIF income is taxed in their hands.
6. Due diligence: they should check the manager's track record across full fund cycles, including defaults and recoveries, and whether the manager invests its own money in the fund.
7. Reasonable conclusion: given their heavy property exposure, a large real estate AIF commitment would worsen concentration. If they want more real estate, a small REIT allocation would add diversification and liquidity instead.

body.title: Choosing an Indirect Real Estate Route
steps: Decide whether you want rental income, growth from developers, or both
Check how much property you already own as a share of net worth
For stocks, review pre-sales, collections, debt and delivery record on screener.in
For funds, check what the index holds and how concentrated it is
For AIFs, confirm the ₹1 crore minimum, lock-in, fees, strategy and manager track record
Keep any single sector fund to a small, deliberate share of your portfolio

points: Developer stocks are bets on selling homes profitably; REITs are bets on rent from completed buildings.
India's 28 big listed developers booked about ₹1.95 lakh crore of sales in FY26, with the top five taking nearly 60%.
Realty stocks swing far more than property prices: the Nifty Realty index moved over 50% between its 52-week low and high.
Realty ETFs and index funds give low-cost exposure to a concentrated basket of developers; a new index fund blends REITs with developers.
Real estate AIFs need ₹1 crore, lock money in for years and mostly lend to developers, with high target returns reflecting high risk.
Choose the route based on whether you want income or growth, and on how much property you already own.
